Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick first-pass guidance below; I’m attaching a starter workbook that lays out the math. I’ve looped in Lauren for procurement and our infra SME (Ben) + Priyom to validate throughput assumptions.

Summary (first pass):
- Traffic assumptions you provided -> peak tokens/sec calculation: using 90 qps * 420 tokens/request = 37,800 tokens/sec at peak.
- We map tokens/sec to GPU capacity using our model performance matrix (attached). For a mid-sized generative model (quantized 34B-ish family) we see ~4,500 tokens/sec/GPU on H100-class instances with our optimized runtime.
- Baseline GPU count = ceil(37,800 / 4,500) = 9 GPUs -> recommend reserving a 10-GPU slab for steady-state to avoid fractional slips.
- Headroom & burst: add 30% buffer for KV cache misses, cold starts, and short bursts -> 10 * 1.3 ≈ 13 GPUs. Recommend a 16-GPU slab for the POC to give a safety cushion and scheduler flexibility (maintenance, canaries, autoscale headroom).
- p95 latency fit: with continuous batching and prefix caching we estimate p95 inference-only ~300–420 ms on the 16-GPU slab for typical payloads; falls within your 500 ms SLO with room for app-side networking.
- Fallback plan: serve a smaller 13B variant on a dedicated 8-GPU slab for longer tails where cost is more important than highest quality.

I'll let Ben confirm the per-GPU tokens/sec for the exact model you plan to use and Priyom to translate into a reserve/commit configuration and monthly cost. Attached: radon_poc_sizing.xlsx (workbook: traffic->slab->cost).

Karthik / team — validated the quick-pass numbers and added a concise procurement blurb. Key outputs below (numbers conservative on purpose):

Assumptions used:
- Model baseline: open-family quantized ~34B (q4o) using Redwood optimized kernels
- Measured throughput: 4,200–4,800 tokens/sec per NVIDIA H100 80GB equivalent in steady conditions (we pick 4,500 tps/GPU for sizing math)
- 13B fallback: ~11,500 tokens/sec per GPU (useful for cost-sensitive fallbacks)

Sizing math (peak steady = 90 qps):
- Peak tokens/sec = 90 * 420 = 37,800 tokens/sec
- GPUs required (steady) = ceil(37,800 / 4,500) = 9 GPUs -> round to 10 for slab hygiene
- Add 30% operational buffer for bursts, cache-miss scenarios, and maintenance -> 10 * 1.3 = 13 GPUs
- Recommendation for POC slab = 16 GPUs. Rationale: clear margin for short bursts to 150 qps, allow for rolling upgrades and canaries, and preserve p95 under noisy neighbor scenarios.

Alternative (cost-constrained):
- Commit to a 10-GPU slab steady and enable vertical burst credit to reach ~13–14 GPUs for short periods (this keeps committed monthly cost lower, but requires strict throttling if sustained).
- Fallback model: run 13B on 8 GPUs for degraded-quality, lower-cost mode; this covers most long-tail traffic and keeps p95 < 800 ms.

Latency & headroom:
- With continuous batching + KV caching + our kernel selection, p95 inference-only on a 16-GPU H100 slab: ~320–380 ms for the 34B quantized model at peak loads. Network + app adds ~60–120 ms depending on routing — still within Radon’s 500 ms SLO.
- Expected headroom: ~25–35% token capacity left when serving normal peak (allows for short unplanned bursts).

Estimated committed cost (3 months, ballpark):
- 16 x H100 reserved slab -> $135k / month (commit tier pricing applied) => ~$405k for 3 months.
- 10 x H100 reserved slab (cost-constrained) -> $86k / month => ~$258k for 3 months.
- Note: prices include reserved GPU capacity + Redwood service fee; exact quote via procurement (Lauren) will include volume discounts and a commit schedule.

Procurement blurb (one-paragraph):
If Radon wants predictable performance during the POC, we recommend reserving a dedicated slab. For a production-like POC with the traffic profile you provided, a 16-GPU H100 slab provides the best balance of latency headroom and burst resilience. If budget is a constraint, a 10-GPU slab with configured burst credits can achieve most steady-state needs but will require throttling during sustained peaks. Contracts are flexible for short-term POCs — we can structure a 3-month reserved commitment with an option to convert into a longer-term commit or downgrade to a smaller reserved slab after the POC with 30 days notice.

- Priyom: can you add the SLA language that applies to dedicated slabs and a short note on what happens if Radon needs an emergency bump during the POC?
